summary: Content-correctness verification of the rewritten footer changelog popup on /scripts. All 7 acceptance criteria from the review request PASS: 9 entries render with correct testids (v1.0.0–v1.8.0), all 9 dates fall between 2026-05-21 and 2026-06-29, ZERO forbidden internal terms leak, APP_VERSION renders as 'v1.8.0', CHANGELOG.md mirrors the JS source, and /scripts /studio /resources /login all load with no compile overlay.

verification_results.changelog_md_matches_js: Both files describe the same 9 entries with identical dates and content. CHANGELOG.md uses humanized month names ('June 29, 2026') while changelog.js uses ISO ('2026-06-29') — semantically equivalent.

critical_code_review_comments: Content is well-scoped to customer voice — no leaks of internal infra (Pinball/Netlify/CSV/GHL/webhooks) detected.
Note: 'HeyGen' appears in 'HeyGen catalog' (v1.6.0) and 'HeyGen avatar' (v1.3.0) — this is explicitly allowed per the review request (HeyGen alone is a product name customers can know).

Minor: changelog.js displays raw ISO date strings (e.g. '2026-06-29') in the popup. Humanizing to 'Jun 29, 2026' (as CHANGELOG.md does) would feel more customer-facing, but this is a polish suggestion — not a defect against the acceptance criteria.
Editing rules comment block at top of changelog.js is clear and binding — good guardrail for future agents.
